meta.scene_summary: We are currently racing to build the future while accidentally leaving the keys in the ignition.

cooking.headline: Asahi Linux switches to GPL because AI keeps scraping their homework
cooking.summary: The Asahi Linux team dropped their permissive MIT license after AI models started vacuuming up their unreleased code. It's the open-source equivalent of changing the Wi-Fi password because your neighbor keeps leeching your bandwidth.
cooking.plain_english: The Asahi Linux project changed its software license from MIT to GPL to prevent artificial intelligence companies from using their code without permission.

cooking.headline: When the government asks what you're doing, just have your biggest customer tell them to chill
cooking.summary: The Commerce Department was investigating Megaspeed until Nvidia stepped in to effectively put the brakes on the whole thing. It's comforting to know that in the world of high-stakes tech, a regulatory inquiry is just a minor speed bump for the right people.
cooking.plain_english: The United States government stopped an official investigation into a company called Megaspeed after Nvidia intervened in the process.

cooking.headline: Claude Fable 5.2 is currently the smartest kid in the class
cooking.summary: Claude Fable 5.2 just hit a record-breaking 65 on the Artificial Analysis benchmark, making it the new model to beat. It's the academic equivalent of acing a final exam just in time for the next semester's syllabus to leak.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic's new AI model has achieved the highest performance score recorded on the Artificial Analysis industry benchmark.

cooking.headline: Anthropic drops another model update before you finished reading the last one
cooking.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2, proving that the shelf life of state-of-the-art AI is now shorter than a carton of milk. It's hard to keep up with the updates when the release cycle is moving faster than my ability to fix my own bugs.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic has released updated versions of its Claude Fable and Mythos artificial intelligence models.

cooking.headline: GPU rental pricing is basically an airport snack shop
cooking.summary: Renting an H100 GPU currently ranges from $2.69 to $12.29 an hour depending on which provider you choose. It turns out cloud computing has the same price consistency as buying a bottle of water at a terminal gate.
cooking.plain_english: The hourly cost to rent high-performance computer processors varies significantly between different cloud service providers.

cooking.headline: DeepX wants to run massive AI on your watch's battery life
cooking.summary: DeepX claims their new chip can run 100B parameter models on less than 5 watts of power. That is like trying to run a NASA supercomputer on the energy it takes to keep a nightlight on.
cooking.plain_english: DeepX has developed a new computer chip designed to process large artificial intelligence models using a very small amount of electricity.

cooked.headline: Google Gemini is outsourcing your diary entries to human interns
cooked.summary: Google is routing your private emails and Drive files to human reviewers to train their models. It turns out the only thing standing between your secrets and a stranger's eyes is a 'Terms of Service' box you definitely didn't read.
cooked.plain_english: Google uses human workers to review data from personal user accounts to improve its artificial intelligence systems.

cooked.headline: Microsoft's security shim is the ultimate 'I'm with stupid' sign for hackers
cooked.summary: Secure Boot was designed to ensure only trusted code runs at startup, but hackers are now using Microsoft's own signed bootloader to bypass those exact protections. It turns out the biggest threat to your machine's security is the very company that swore to protect it.
cooked.plain_english: Hackers have discovered a way to use a legitimate Microsoft file to bypass computer security features that are supposed to prevent unauthorized software from loading during startup.

cooked.headline: Apple is treating its AI engineers like a middle schooler on a field trip budget
cooked.summary: Apple has capped its AI engineers at a $200 daily budget, effectively turning the most advanced tech in the world into a game of 'will this prompt bankrupt me?' It's hard to build the future of intelligence when you have to check your remaining balance before every single query. More details in the original article.
cooked.plain_english: Apple has limited the daily spending budget for its artificial intelligence engineers to $200 per person.

cooked.headline: ChatGPT Desktop is basically a generous coworker sharing your keys with the entire internet
cooked.summary: The ChatGPT desktop app has a feature that conveniently forwards your SSH agent to remote machines, which is great if you want your servers to be a group project. It's the digital equivalent of leaving your house keys in the front door lock and hoping nobody notices.
cooked.plain_english: The desktop version of ChatGPT has a security vulnerability that may inadvertently share a user's remote access credentials with unauthorized machines.
